entities.title: Every typed operation calls the JSON layer
entities.summary: A typed operation writes its operands as UTV JSON, calls the 0.2 function and reads the answer back, rather than computing on the Rust fields.
entities.context: docs/library-api.md section 2: every typed operation must agree with the JSON-level everyday API, and so with the shared fixtures; implementations should call the 0.2 functions underneath rather than re-implement them.
entities.decision: The typed layer has no arithmetic of its own. Constructors validate by reading their own JSON back (read_as over read_civil), and operations call ops::add, ops::fields, ops::days_between, ops::contains, ops::overlaps, zones::resolve, zones::to_zone and text::parse_text / format_text.
entities.rationale: "Every operation calls the 0.2 JSON layer underneath, so the typed layer and the shared fixtures can't disagree" (typed/mod.rs). The cost is a JSON round trip per call.

entities.title: Constructors return Result<T, Diagnostics>
entities.summary: of(...) returns Result, so there is no panicking Of and no separate TryOf.
entities.context: The library contract has a raising Of and a non-raising TryOf. Rust has no exceptions.
entities.decision: Every constructor that can refuse (of, of_hms, of_hms_nano, at_offset, Interval::of, of_ratio) returns Result<T, Diagnostics>; Diagnostics implements std::error::Error, so ? works in a main returning Result<(), Box<dyn Error>>.
entities.rationale: "Rust has no exceptions, so its of returns Result<T, Diagnostics>" (docs/library-api.md section 1); the README says the same.

entities.title: The clamping month arithmetic is a separate method
entities.summary: add_months_constrained and add_years_constrained are their own methods, and add_with(Period, MonthEnd) takes a policy.
entities.context: The contract's total overload AddMonths(n, MonthEnd.Constrain) must reject MonthEnd.Reject, because a policy can't change the return type. Rust has no overloads.
entities.decision: add_months(n) and add_years(n) reject and return an Outcome; add_months_constrained(n) and add_years_constrained(n) clamp and return the value; add(Period) rejects and add_with(Period, MonthEnd) takes either policy and returns an Outcome.
entities.rationale: "Rust: no overloads, so the total forms are separate methods" (docs/library-api.md section 6); a Reject policy can't be passed where a plain value is returned (README).

entities.title: Total operations panic beyond i128
entities.summary: A total operation whose result leaves the i128 range panics, the way integer overflow does in Rust; constructors refuse such values up front.
entities.context: Total operations return plain values, but the JSON layer answers unsupported (implementation-limit) when arithmetic leaves i128. A plain value has no room for that answer.
entities.decision: total() panics with the operation, status and diagnostics if the JSON layer refuses; constructors refuse years whose day numbers or local seconds leave i128 with implementation-limit.
entities.rationale: "Total operations that would leave this library's i128 range panic, the way integer overflow does in Rust" (typed/mod.rs; total's # Panics section).

entities.title: Ord only where rules can't change the order, and in agreement with Eq
entities.summary: Ord is implemented for every type whose order is rule-free, with ties broken by representation; ZonedIntent has none.
entities.context: Rust requires Ord to agree with Eq, but equality is representation (09:30 is not 09:30:00) while the contract compares a missing second as 0. And a < on two values must not exist unless it can say "unknown" (implementations/README.md, Idiomatic APIs).
entities.decision: Compare with a missing second as 0, then put the value without a second first (CivilTime::key); FixedOffsetDateTime orders by instant, then offset, then wall time. ZonedIntent implements no Ord; TemporalContext::compare answers Outcome<Ordering>.
entities.rationale: "Where a language requires ordering to agree with equality (Rust's Ord ...), ties between equal times break by representation" (docs/library-api.md section 1); the README's Order paragraph says the same.
